whatThisFileIs: An R1 authorship claim, and nothing else. It says who wrote the compliance-path files below and on which issue. It asserts nothing about whether they are correct, and it carries no `reviews[]` entry.
doesNotClaimR2: There is no `reviews[]` entry here and there will not be one from me. R2 wants a named reviewer who is not the author, and I am the author of every path above. Reviewer designation for a Coder compliance-path commit is the CTO (MediaTech). There is no independent security reviewer on this team (board declined the seat on cost), so a CTO review is a recorded degradation, not independent review -- stated here rather than implied. The CTO verdict on AFC-502 is APPROVE (land), recorded as a `Reviewed-by:` trailer on the commit this claim covers. Writing a `reviews[]` entry naming myself would turn a control into a rubber stamp. This migration touches transfers/marriage/minutes/tasks/announcements/referrals tables (personal data, including minors) and the Directus grant ceiling, so per the Coder instructions it goes to the CTO regardless.
scopeOfTheClaim: R1 only: authorship of the listed paths on AFC-477 (Slice 3f office bundle: transfers, marriage_matters, office_minutes + minutes_attendees M2M, tasks, announcements, event_referrals + five per-domain audit tables, conditional §9.6 events deltas, event_sessions deferred as a documented choice, suite 79 tables/rerun/constraints/links/guards/indexes/rollback-refusal contract). It is not clearance of the retention gate (plan 0.10.5), which only the CEO can clear. Non-compliance-path files changed on the same issue (office API routes, office server util, shared office zod + feed helper, office/calendar/search UI pages, web contract test) are ordinary code, committed separately without this claim, not claimed here.
whatTheChangeActuallyDoes: New migration creating transfers (§9.1: person, from/to branch differ, zone denorm via from_branch, lifecycle requested/approved/completed/rejected), marriage_matters (§9.2: person + nullable partner, branch required, zone denorm), office_minutes + minutes_attendees (§9.3: title/date/body/file/status, M2M minute→person/user with at-least-one-side CHECK), tasks (§9.4: title/description, assignee_user XOR/OR assignee_person required, branch + zone, due_date, status, priority, polymorphic related_type/related_id with no FK), announcements (§9.5: title/body, publish window ordered CHECK, channels/audience jsonb, lifecycle draft/scheduled/published/cancelled, branch nullable = area-wide), event_referrals (§9.7: event, inviter, invitee_name required, branch/zone scope copy), plus five per-domain audit tables (transfer/marriage/minute/task/announcement events, parent CASCADE) following the welfare_case_events precedent. Conditional §9.6 events deltas (overview, invite_a_friend_enabled default false, attendance_session + FK where attendance_sessions exists), NOTICE-loud skips where absent; blessings_total stays derived via Flow, not a column; event_sessions deferred to the Summit slice. Branch RESTRICT / person RESTRICT / denorm SET NULL / audit CASCADE; backfills zone from branch where known. Grants: directus_app SELECT everywhere, INSERT/UPDATE operational columns only, NO DELETE anywhere; REVOKE ALL FROM PUBLIC on all 12 tables; no roles minted (ADR-0002). Rollback refuses while any office/audit table holds rows; drops the events FK added here and all 12 tables children-first, no CASCADE; events delta columns intentionally left on the surviving table (documented, F1-safe). tests/db/79 proves tables, rerun-stability, the full constraint matrix (status enums, branches-differ, window order, attendee/assignee presence), denorm backfill + RESTRICT/CASCADE shape, the app-identity ceiling, the §9 index set, and rollback refusal.
